I have been working this land for 50 years, so I know what it can do. My 5 mu is not big, but cotton has been my main crop for a long time. Mungbean I plant on maybe half a mu on the edge where the soil is poorer — it does not need much and the family eats some, sells the rest.

For cotton, I use the improved Bt variety like most people in Quzhou. The old varieties get eaten by bollworm too badly. I buy seed from the same dealer in town — my neighbor Old Wang said the 33B type did well last year. I plant about 4.5 mu of cotton.

For fertilizer on cotton, I follow what I did last year, which worked. I put about 2 bags of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base before planting, that is about 50 kg per mu, so roughly 7-8 kg each of N, P, K per mu from that. Then at bud stage and flowering I top-dress urea, maybe 15 kg per mu total across two applications. Altogether nitrogen comes to about 20 kg per mu. Phosphorus and potassium I do not add extra beyond the compound — too expensive and my soil here is not bad for those.

Cotton needs water. I irrigate from the well 4 times — once before planting if dry, then at bud, flowering, and boll-filling. Pesticide is the big worry. Even with Bt cotton I still spray 7-8 times for aphids, mites, lygus bugs. Cannot skip this or the harvest is ruined. I plough the field in winter then rotary till in spring.

Last year I got about 270 kg seed cotton per mu. I expect similar this year if weather is normal.

Mungbean is easy. 0.5 mu, traditional local seed I save myself, no need to buy. Mungbean makes its own nitrogen so I only put a little compound fertilizer at planting, maybe 10 kg per mu. One irrigation if it is very dry at flowering, otherwise rainfed. Spray maybe once for bean fly. Light rotary tilling. I get around 120 kg per mu usually.
